target_customer: Parents in US metro areas who pay a monthly membership for credits to book kids classes and activities, plus activity providers who list classes
problem: Parents struggle to find and book good children's activities, and providers struggle to fill classes and manage registration and payments.
business_model: Subscription membership with credits (from about 49 dollars a month) plus marketplace take from providers and provider software

founders.name: Solomon Liou
founders.background_notes: Listed as founder and CEO on the YC page. Started the company after becoming a parent (TechCrunch 2017).

founders.name: Chhay Chhun
founders.background_notes: YC bio reads dad, husband, co-founder and CTO, Harvard 02.

founders.name: Aaron Kaufman
founders.background_notes: Listed as founder on the YC page.

competitors.name: Sawyer
competitors.what: Booking platform for kids classes and activities

competitors.name: The Kid's Passport
competitors.what: New York subscription letting kids try five classes a month for 99 dollars

technical_complexity.rationale: A two sided booking marketplace with membership credits, provider scheduling and payments; standard web and mobile engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Local supply of providers gave some marketplace effect, but provider relationships were not exclusive and competitors such as Sawyer targeted the same providers.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No large player copied it in sourced material. KidPass bought Mommy Nearest in September 2019 and was itself bought by BEGiN in August 2021.

market_need_then: TechCrunch 2017 reported 20,000 families signed up, over 100,000 activities booked, over 3,000 NYC subscribers, 20 to 30 percent monthly growth and over 900 providers, indicating real early demand.

branding.domain_note: Used kidpass.com, which now redirects to the BEGiN site.

identity.voice_and_tone: Parent friendly, positioned as the ClassPass for kids

branding.community_and_virality: Local press such as Time Out New York and amNY covered it; no evidence of merch or fan community.

brand_strength.rationale: Descriptive pass concept easy to grasp and good local press, but similar names exist such as Kids Pass in the UK and Little Passports.

outcome_analysis: KidPass launched in New York in 2016, raised a seed and a 5.1 million dollar Series A in 2017 and expanded to other metros. It added media by buying Mommy Nearest in 2019, then sold to BEGiN in August 2021, reaching over a million parents and 5,000 providers by then. The price is undisclosed and total raised is unclear, so the exit looks like a consolidation by a kids education company after pandemic disruption, though no source states a reason.
notes: Seed of 1.2 million in 2016-09 comes from the EdSurge headline and search summary (the page itself returned 404) and is consistent with a StartupIntros entry; investors from that summary. Aggregators disagree on totals (16.25 million over 10 rounds vs 5.5 million), so later rounds, including a possible 2019 round, are unverified. Olivia Ballve is named as a founder by TechCrunch 2017 but not on the YC page, so not listed. The Kid's Passport article is dated 2016-01 and the competitor is described only via a search summary. Acquirer BEGiN and date per its press release.
